faqs.question: What's a good Halloween riddle for a 5-year-old?
faqs.answer: Try a rhyme with one picture clue: "I am orange, round and fat, I sit on the step with a stem for a hat. What am I?" The answer is a pumpkin. Set 1 on this page has 6 riddles pitched at ages 5 to 7, all with plain clues and no scary images.

faqs.question: How do I give a riddle hint without spoiling the answer?
faqs.answer: Tell a simpler riddle that uses the same trick, then go back to the hard one. In a 2024 Communications Psychology study, 15.6% of people solved a riddle cold but 34% solved it after an analogous riddle, and they answered in about 75 seconds instead of 210.

faqs.question: Are these Halloween riddles original?
faqs.answer: Yes. All 30 riddles were written for this page and checked against SubhSandesh's other Halloween posts so none repeats a line. The Exeter Book lines quoted in the history section are Old English originals over 1,000 years old, given only as short quotations.

faqs.question: What is the oldest riddle in English?
faqs.answer: The oldest surviving English riddles are the roughly 95 Old English riddles in the Exeter Book, a late 10th-century manuscript held at Exeter Cathedral Library since 1072. One riddle in the collection also survives in the 9th-century Northumbrian Leiden Riddle, according to The Riddle Ages.

faqs.question: Why do people love solving riddles?
faqs.answer: Solving one usually brings an "aha" moment, and that feeling is rewarding. In 2025 experiments by Mercier and colleagues, people given insight riddles were 25% more likely to choose another problem, and those who felt a stronger aha were more willing to share the riddle.

faqs.question: Did the Exeter Book riddles come with answers?
faqs.answer: No. The manuscript prints no solutions, so every answer you see in a modern edition is a scholar's guess. Some are still argued over: John D. Niles traced nine proposed answers for Riddle 74, from a cuttlefish to a quill pen.

faqs.question: How many riddles do I need for a Halloween party?
faqs.answer: Plan on one to two minutes per riddle, including the reveal. Ten riddles fill roughly 10 to 20 minutes, which suits a break between games; all 30 here would take 30 to 60 minutes.

faqs.question: Are these riddles hard enough for adults?
faqs.answer: Set 3's logic riddles and set 4's wordplay riddles work for adults at a family table, but they are deliberately fair rather than fiendish. Adults who want lateral-thinking puzzles with misleading set-ups need a harder list than this all-ages one.

faqs.question: Can I send a Halloween riddle to someone who lives far away?
faqs.answer: Yes. Put the riddle in a letter on an interactive Halloween card and make the answer the word carved on the pumpkin, or hide it in the sealed P.S. of the premium page. Both open in any phone or laptop browser from a private link.

faqs.question: When is Halloween in 2026 and 2027?
faqs.answer: Halloween is on 31 October every year. In 2026 it falls on a Saturday and in 2027 on a Sunday.

# Halloween Riddles With Answers: 30 New Ones, Easy to Tricky

Here are 30 original Halloween riddles with answers in four sets: 6 rhyming ones for ages 5–7, 8 "What am I?" riddles for ages 8–11, 8 logic riddles for teens and families, and 8 wordplay riddles. Each answer sits in italics after its riddle, so you can cover it with a thumb.

That layout matters on a small screen. 48.3% of the pages shared on SubhSandesh are opened on a phone, and the average page is viewed 11.1 times, so a riddle someone receives is usually read more than once. Below them: an age table, three studies on the "aha" of solving, the Exeter Book riddles that had no answer key, and how to send one riddle on 31 October (Saturday in 2026, Sunday in 2027).

## What is a Halloween riddle?

A Halloween riddle is a short puzzle that describes a spooky or seasonal thing in disguise and asks the listener to name it. A fair one never lies: every clue is true, but the obvious reading points somewhere else.

Riddles are far older than Halloween. Searching the Yale eHRAF ethnographic database, Marius Mercier, Alexis Garsmeur and Hugo Mercier found riddles reported in 43 cultures on every continent, including 18 of 60 largely unrelated small-scale societies, in a [2025 paper accepted by *Psychology of Aesthetics, Creativity, and the Arts*](https://osf.io/preprints/psyarxiv/arn2h_v2).

## 30 original Halloween riddles with answers, in 4 sets

Every riddle below was written for this page. The sets get harder as you scroll.

### 1. Easy rhyming riddles for ages 5–7 (6 riddles)

- I am orange, round and fat, I sit on the step with a stem for a hat. What am I? *Answer: a pumpkin.*
- I wear a pointy hat, I ride a broom, and my black cat follows me round the room. Who am I? *Answer: a witch.*
- I float through doors and I say "boo", and my white sheet trails behind me too. What am I? *Answer: a ghost.*
- You carry me from door to door, and I get heavier at every house. What am I? *Answer: your trick-or-treat bucket.*
- I am wrapped from my head to my toes, but nobody unwraps me on a birthday. What am I? *Answer: a mummy.*
- People knock on me all night on 31 October, but nobody ever comes to see me. What am I? *Answer: a front door.*

### 2. "What am I?" riddles for ages 8–11 (8 riddles)

- I have 206 parts once I'm grown, I'm inside every one of you, and on Halloween I'm a costume too. What am I? *Answer: a skeleton.*
- I'm round and sticky, I'm made of silk, and I catch my dinner without moving. What am I? *Answer: a spider's web.*
- I'm scooped out by the spoonful, I'm stringy and slimy, and I'm full of seeds you can roast. What am I? *Answer: the inside of a pumpkin.*
- I have two hands but no fingers, and at midnight both of my hands point straight up. What am I? *Answer: a clock.*
- I sweep the kitchen floor all year, but on one night the stories say I fly. What am I? *Answer: a broomstick.*
- I follow you down every street on Halloween, I copy every move you make, and I vanish when the porch lamp is switched off. What am I? *Answer: your shadow.*
- I hoot in the dark, I turn my head almost all the way round, and I'm awake while you sleep. What am I? *Answer: an owl.*
- I'm sweet and I crunch, and I'm shaped like a tiny cone in yellow, orange and white. What am I? *Answer: candy corn.*

### 3. Logic riddles for teens and families (8 riddles)

- A witch has 3 cats, and each cat has 3 kittens. How many cats live in the witch's house? *Answer: 12.*
- A street has 20 houses. Every house with a pumpkin outside also has its porch light on, and 12 houses have lights on. What is the most pumpkins the street could have? *Answer: 12.*
- This year 31 October is a Saturday, and the coming February has no 29th. Which weekday will next 31 October land on? *Answer: Sunday, since a 365-day year is 52 weeks plus one spare day.*
- Which letter appears once in "October", twice in "Halloween" and never in "pumpkin"? *Answer: E.*
- Count the legs: 2 witches, 3 black cats and 1 spider. *Answer: 24 (4 + 12 + 8).*
- A ghost drifts through one wall a minute. A haunted house is a row of 5 rooms with a wall between each pair. How long from the first room to the last? *Answer: 4 minutes, since 5 rooms have 4 walls between them.*
- Tomorrow is All Saints' Day. What day is today? *Answer: Halloween, 31 October.*
- My first is in "bat" but not in "cat", and my second and third sit side by side in "moon". What do I shout? *Answer: boo.*

### 4. Wordplay riddles: drop a letter or flip a meaning (8 riddles)

Six delete the first letter of a Halloween word; two use a word with two meanings. Save them for confident spellers.

- I'm a spirit in a white sheet; take away my first letter and I throw the party. *Answer: ghost, then host.*
- I fly on a broom; take away my first letter and you'll want to scratch. *Answer: witch, then itch.*
- A vampire wears me round his shoulders; take away my first letter and I swing through the trees. *Answer: cape, then ape.*
- A werewolf does me at the moon; take away my first letter and I hoot back from a branch. *Answer: howl, then owl.*
- A haunted house tries to give you me; take away my first letter and I'm what a good friend shows you. *Answer: scare, then care.*
- I'm what you feel when a skeleton jumps out; take away my first letter and I'm the opposite of wrong. *Answer: fright, then right.*
- I fly out of a cave at dusk, and in cricket you swing me at the ball. *Answer: bat.*
- Witches cast me, and you do me to a word one letter at a time. *Answer: spell.*

## Which Halloween riddle set suits which group?

This table compares the four sets. Ages and wait times are editorial guidance, not measured norms.

| Set | Suggested ages | Wait before first hint | What solving takes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Easy rhymes (6) | 5–7 | 20 seconds | Picturing one familiar thing |
| 2. "What am I?" (8) | 8–11 | 60 seconds | Combining 3 clues |
| 3. Logic (8) | 12 to adult | 2 minutes | Counting or ruling options out |
| 4. Wordplay (8) | 10+, confident spellers | 90 seconds | Spotting a hidden second word |

With mixed ages, open with set 2 and save set 4 for last. At one to two minutes a riddle, all 30 fill 30 to 60 minutes.

## Why does solving a riddle feel so good?

That jolt is insight, the "aha" moment when your view of a problem suddenly reorganises. Three studies show why it matters.

- **People want more after an aha.** In the first of Mercier and colleagues' five experiments (197 US adults), insight riddles raised the chance of choosing one more problem by 25% compared with step-by-step problems, and stronger ahas went with more willingness to share.
- **A "sister" riddle is the best hint.** In a [2024 *Communications Psychology* study](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC11332086), 15.6% of participants solved a riddle cold, against 34% after an analogous riddle whose answer they had found or been shown. Correct answers came in about 75 seconds instead of 210.
- **Aha answers stick.** A [2013 *Psychological Research* study](https://europepmc.org/article/MED/23007629) gave 50 people magic tricks to explain; 14 days later they recalled 64.4% of solutions reached with an aha, against 52.4% without one.

So do not reveal an answer early. When someone is stuck, tell an easier riddle with the same trick, then return to the hard one.

## The oldest English riddles came with no answers

The Exeter Book, a late 10th-century manuscript, holds about 95 Old English riddles among roughly 130 poems, according to [The Riddle Ages](https://theriddleages.com/riddles/collection/the-exeter-book-riddles/about/), an AHRC-funded scholarly site from the University of Birmingham. Bishop Leofric bequeathed it to Exeter Cathedral Library in 1072, and it gives no solutions, so every modern answer is a scholar's guess.

Riddle 47 opens "Moððe word fræt", "a moth ate words", and describes a thief in the darkness that swallows a man's song yet grows no wiser; the usual answer is a book-moth. Andrew Higl, in the [*American Journal of Play* in spring 2017](https://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/EJ1153368.pdf), notes that John D. Niles traced nine proposed answers for Riddle 74, whose speaker lies dead among fishes, from a cuttlefish to a quill pen.

## Sending a Halloween riddle to one person

SubhSandesh's Halloween pages are one-person greeting pages, not a party quiz tool. For one person, a partner, best friend or niece abroad, they make the recipient guess before the reveal.

On [the interactive Halloween card](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween), put your riddle in the letter and make its answer the word carved on the pumpkin, which glows once the candle lights. It takes about 5 minutes, holds up to six photos, and has a Kids tone with no gore or jump scares. For a harder riddle, [the premium Halloween page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) takes about 10 minutes: hide the answer in the sealed P.S., set an optional unlock time, and collect their guess through the reply box, up to 280 characters, emailed to you.

If the answer is a private joke, add a password; 38.5% of SubhSandesh creators do (2,000 of 5,199). For a partner who prefers questions, [the Court of Love page](https://subhsandesh.in/court-of-love) puts them on trial with 10 funny questions; it is not Halloween-themed.

## When a riddle list is the wrong choice

- **Under-5s.** Only 6 riddles here are pitched below age 8; a picture hunt suits toddlers better.
- **New English speakers.** All 8 wordplay riddles depend on English spelling, so start learners on set 3.
- **A crowd of 20 or more.** The Halloween pages carry one name and one answer, so print the riddles or read them aloud.

## Sources

- Mercier, Garsmeur and Mercier (2025), *The Appeal of Insight*, accepted manuscript.
- Bieth et al. (2024), Communications Psychology, 7 June 2024.
- Danek et al. (2013), Psychological Research (abstract only).
- Higl (2017), *Riddle Hero*, American Journal of Play 9(3).
- The Riddle Ages, *The Exeter Book Riddles* (undated).
